Chapter 7: Overcoming Common Barriers and Staying Motivated
Let's be honest—no matter how committed you are, obstacles will pop up along the way. Maybe you’re dealing with fatigue, a packed schedule, a dip in motivation, or just one of those unpredictable life moments. The real trick? Recognizing these barriers and having some go-to strategies ready so you can keep your strength training on track for the long haul.
One of the biggest challenges I hear about is just not having enough time. Sound familiar? That’s where the five-minute approach comes in handy. But you can get even more creative—try splitting movement into smaller chunks. Maybe you squeeze in two minutes before breakfast and three after dinner. It all adds up!
Then there are those days when motivation just isn’t there—when your energy’s low or your progress feels stuck. In those moments, it helps to pause and remember why you started in the first place. Maybe it’s wanting more independence, a better mood, or just the energy to enjoy your favorite activities. Visual reminders can really help—a sticky note on your fridge, or a photo of someone you love, can give you that extra nudge when you need it most.
Don’t forget about the power of social support. Sharing your goals with a friend or family member, joining a group, or even connecting with folks online can make a huge difference. And those small wins? Celebrate them! Whether you’ve completed a week of routines or just noticed your day-to-day tasks are getting a little easier, every bit of progress builds momentum.
Sometimes, physical limitations or setbacks can get in the way. If a certain movement starts to feel uncomfortable, just swap it out for something that works the same muscles. And if you’re dealing with illness or traveling, be gentle with yourself—come back to your routine when you can, focusing on consistency over intensity.
Here are a few gentle, practical strategies to help you overcome those tough moments:
First, break routines into smaller parts when time or energy is tight. Second, lean on visual cues and reminders to keep your motivation alive. Third, reach out to friends, family, or community groups for support. Fourth, take time to celebrate your small achievements—they really do matter. And finally, adapt your routines as needed so they fit your life, not the other way around.
When you anticipate these barriers and meet them with flexibility and a little self-compassion, it gets so much easier to stick with your practice. Remember, this journey isn’t about being perfect—it’s about showing up for yourself, staying persistent, and treating yourself with kindness along the way.
